desc:
A positive integer is called ugly when its only prime factors are 2, 3 and 5. The number 1 has no prime factors at all, so it counts as ugly. Zero and negative numbers are never ugly.

Return true if n is ugly and false otherwise.

n = 6   -> true   (2 * 3)
n = 14  -> false  (2 * 7, and 7 is not allowed)
n = 1   -> true

This is the building block for the next question about listing ugly numbers in order.
hints: Handle non-positive numbers first. What should happen for 0 and for negative values?
If n is ugly, you can keep dividing it by 2 while it is divisible, then by 3, then by 5.
After removing every factor 2, 3 and 5, the number is ugly exactly when what is left equals 1.
editorial: Return false for n ≤ 0. Otherwise strip all factors of 2, then of 3, then of 5 by repeated division. Whatever remains is the part of n made of other primes: it is 1 when n is ugly and larger than 1 otherwise.

Each division at least halves n, so there are at most about 31 divisions in total. The time is O(log n) and the space is O(1). Do not try to factorize n completely with trial division up to its square root; that is far slower than needed.
